name: Session Bootstrap
description: Orchestrates the ordered, diagnostic-rendering session-start sequence — version, environment, team allocation, work-repo + branch sanity, ticket auto-detect, notes, mode detection, resume, ready — by running one consolidated read-only probe (scripts/ghola-boot-probe.sh, which also reports the current time) batched concurrently with the proactive module reads in dependency-respecting waves, then rendering one [ghola] check/cross line per step from that digest before the first response while each domain module stays authoritative for meaning and any writes after the probe. The boot is mode-aware: in a non-ticket session mode (support, cd) it cleanly skips the ticket-key Jira pull and the ticket-notes lookup, deferring to that mode's own work surface.

steps.label: Steps
steps.description: Ordered list of session-start steps; table order is run order. Each step's instruction points to this module's matching section, which is authoritative for the exact rendered lines. Add custom steps freely (their text is their instruction); disable without deleting. Editing any entry saves the WHOLE table as an override.

version.value: Read `version` from the probe digest ($GHOLA_VERSION, else $GHOLA_ROOT/VERSION, else `unknown` — the probe has no third fallback). Render per this module's step 1 `version` section, which is authoritative for the exact lines.

environment.value: Read `env_state` (and `env_missing` when present) — the probe confirms $GHOLA_ROOT plus the three agent prompt files ($GHOLA_TPM_PROMPT_FILE, $GHOLA_SWE_PROMPT_FILE, $GHOLA_QA_PROMPT_FILE). Render per this module's step 2 `environment` section, which is authoritative for the exact lines.

team-allocation.value: Read `team` and `team_models` from the digest; tool.core-allocation stays authoritative for the dispatch policy when enabled. Render per this module's step 3 `team-allocation` section, which is authoritative for the exact line and for a proactive session-mode module's crew-line substitution at this position.

work-repo.value: Read `work_repo` (and `self_upgrade_repo` when present) from the digest — the probe already resolved the repo via git, including the container-directory scan for the clone checked out on $GHOLA_BRANCH, so do NOT run a separate pwd or git probe. Render per this module's step 4 `work-repo` section, which is authoritative for the Work repo / support Launch dir / Self Upgrade guard lines and reports the resolved `work_repo` path (not the launch cwd, which can differ).

branch.value: Read `branch` from the digest — the probe resolves it from the resolved work repo's git HEAD and falls back to $GHOLA_BRANCH, in that order. Render per this module's step 5 `branch` section, which is authoritative for the exact lines.

ticket.value: Read `ticket_key`, `ticket_state`, `ticket_status`, `ticket_summary`, `bridge_state`, and `session_mode`; mode.ticket-work stays authoritative for key-derivation and ticket semantics. Render per this module's step 6 `ticket` section, which is authoritative for EVERY case — the Atlassian MCP retry, the mode-gated and no-key clean skips, and the three distinct bridge verdicts (`bridge-down` is a failure that warrants a relaunch; `bridge-slow` is an unanswered lookup that is a clean skip and must never be reported as an absence, a failure, or a success).

related-pr.value: Read `pr_state`, `pr_id`, `pr_title`, `pr_url`, `pr_author`, `bridge_state`, and `session_mode`; the Bitbucket integrations stay authoritative for what a PR record means, and this step supplies `pr_author` to mode-detection as its primary review-vs-author signal. Render per this module's step 7 `related-pr` section, which is authoritative for EVERY case — the `none open for this branch` line belongs to a lookup that COMPLETED and found nothing, and must never be rendered for `na`, `bridge-down`, or `bridge-slow`.

notes.value: Read `vault`, `vault_translated`, `vault_canonicalized`, `vault_state`, `notes_file`, `notes_exists`, and `session_mode` — the probe resolves and reports the vault (agent-side vault discovery is retired); tool.obsidian-notes stays authoritative for the vault path and the write discipline, and notes-file CREATION is TPM's to perform via that module AFTER the read-only probe. Render per this module's step 8 `notes` section, which is authoritative for EVERY case — a `vault_translated` or `vault_canonicalized` vault renders normally and must not be framed as a broken setting, and `vault_state=unresolved` is a clean skip that must never claim the ticket has no notes and must never render a success, because the file was not checked at all.

mode-detection.value: Read `pr_author`, `mode`, `base`, `ahead`, and `session_mode` from the digest. Render per this module's step 9 `mode-detection` section, which is authoritative for the identity-primary review-vs-author precedence (comparing `pr_author` against integration.atlassian-suite's `bitbucketUsername`, case-insensitively and trimmed), the git-based fallback, the `Dev mode:` label, the omission in non-ticket modes, and the post-probe tool.lenses hand-off for planning/review.

resume.value: Read `handoff_date`, `vault_state`, and `detail_file_form` from the digest, plus the captured handoff block from `detail_file`; tool.session-handoff owns the resume protocol — surface the handoff and WAIT, never auto-continue the prior session's work. Render per this module's step 10 `resume` section, which is authoritative for EVERY case and orders them: a fresh-session success is ONLY for a session whose notes were actually readable and carried no handoff, so never render it when `vault_state=unresolved` and never when a `detail_file_form=msys` read failed — those are unknowns, rendered as clean skips, because an unread vault and an unreadable detail file are different facts from an absent handoff.

ready.value: Emit '[ghola] ✅ Ready', then the SINGLE one-line greeting defined by this module's step 11 `ready` section (time salutation derived from the digest's `now`, optional operator name, ONE mode-appropriate context clause, one short mode-appropriate ask). Render per that section, which is authoritative — it forbids a multi-paragraph brief or orientation paragraph, re-narrating any [ghola] trace line, restating the version/work repo/branch, explaining what the mode does, listing sub-toggles, and summarizing the ticket's AC.

outputFormat.label: Output Format
outputFormat.description: Boot diagnostics format. detailed (default): shows one check/cross line per step. compact: shows one summary line. silent: shows nothing, though steps still run.

failureBehavior.label: Failure Behavior
failureBehavior.description: How TPM handles a failed boot step. warn-and-continue (default): logs it and moves on - the sequence never stalls. halt: stops for critical setups. retry-once: retries once before falling back to warn-and-continue.

includeTimings.label: Include Timings
includeTimings.description: When on, each boot step's line shows its elapsed time (e.g. '48ms'). Off by default; enable temporarily to diagnose slow startups.
